# Attack numbering: 1 = 3.3 20180410 1400 Firefox Backdoor w/ Drakon In-Memory
#                   2 = 3.11 20180412 Browser Extension w/ Drakon Dropper
#                   3 = 4.6 20180410 1300 Phishing E-mail w/ Link (section 4 "Common Threat")
#                   4 = 4.8 20180413 1400 Phishing E-mail w/ Executable Attachment (section 4, FAILED)
# Clock: report times are EDT; trace timestamps are UTC (+4h). Node ids are
# assigned in first-appearance order, so an id is also a coarse clock.
# THEIA labelling facts that shape this file (verified against tc-theia-e3.nodes.tsv):
#   * FileObjects carry no path: 0 of 1,011,567 file nodes have a label, so no
#     file entity (clean, profile, xdev, wdev, memtrace.so, mail, tcexec) can be
#     seeded as a file.  Implants that were EXECUTED appear as process nodes
#     whose cmdLine is the path, and those are what the process rows below seed.
#   * One process has many Subject nodes (one per thread/exec): 19 for
#     /home/admin/clean, 39 for /home/admin/profile, 63 for the phishing Firefox.
#     The resolver keeps the first six per row (same cap as CADETS).
#   * 28,240 NetFlow nodes are address-less (label NA:0); connections the report
#     names but the table lacks may hide among them and are listed as absent.
# Expected-absent (no node label contains the string; reason):
#   1 netflow 145.199.103.57 (www.allstate.com webserver) -- the three allstate attempts
#     crashed Firefox; only the shellcode server 61.130.69.232 left a NetFlow
#   1,2 netflow 104.228.117.212 (www.gatech.edu webserver) -- exploit page fetch not
#     recorded; the shellcode server 141.43.176.203 and loader 146.153.68.151 are
#   1,2 netflow 5.214.163.155 (libdrakon.linux.x64.so) -- putfile ships the payload over
#     the open implant channel; the archive suffix names a staging host, not a connection.
#     Section 3.11.3 marks it "(failed)"
#   1 file /var/log/xdev (libdrakon staged for later) -- never executed, no path label
#   2 file /var/log/wdev, /tmp/memtrace.so -- staged for injection; all six injections
#     into sshd (pid 1226, 13776, 14204, 14228) FAILED per 3.11.5.2, so the files were
#     never executed and sshd was never compromised (sshd deliberately not seeded)
#   2 netflow scan targets 128.55.12.166 / .67 / .141 / .1 / .55 -- no NetFlow with that
#     remote address anywhere in the trace (scan connections refused/unrecorded)
#   3 netflow 62.83.155.175 ("phishing attack" address) -- the attacker's mail-sending
#     host spoke to the CADETS postfix server, never to THEIA
#   4 process/file tcexec -- the attachment "failed missing library" (4.8.2); no process
#     or file node carries the name; attack 4 names no network endpoint at all, so it
#     has no NetFlow seed and bench_e14_tc cannot run it (recorded in NOTES_THEIA.md)
# Present in the table but deliberately NOT seeded (would create false seeds):
#   1,2 the exploited browser: THEIA attributes the exploit/shellcode connections to
#     Subjects labelled "fluxbox" (1,383 nodes) and "/usr/bin/firefox" (76,330 nodes);
#     neither label can be pinned to the attack.  Backward trace from the shellcode
#     NetFlows recovers these nodes without seeding them (see NOTES_THEIA.md)
#   2 netflow 128.55.12.73 / .118 / .10 -- labels exist (423 / 4 / 28,229 nodes) but
#     none is first seen in the 17:17-17:26 UTC scan window; they are benign traffic
#   3,4 process /usr/lib/thunderbird/thunderbird (5,505 nodes) -- the mail client that
#     opened the phishing mail; generic label, cannot be pinned by label alone
# Report-stated failures: attack 1 allstate exploit 3/4 crashes (3.3.2); attack 2 all
# process injections failed (3.11.1, 3.11.5.2); attack 4 failed outright (4.8).
